payload.text: Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 150 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Buenas tardes. He escuchado su cifra. La mía es otra: La Casa Encendida, ciento trece P. Ése es mi término hoy.

¡Ay, hijo, qué alegría! Three pages full already, and churros promised — you spoil this old woman. My grandchildren still hunt the Taxi Blanco, and I have one here for you: twelve P, cariño.

A little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates! ¿Has comido?
Señor, eighty-one is one céntimo of vanity too many. Eighty pesetas — a round, elegant number, fit for El Marqués and for Salamanca. Give me your hand, por favor, and let the afternoon rest.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Perrito con Abrigo, 5 P. Made for beginners.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — El Marqués, mira that foil! Seventy-three pesos, for you, today only. And listen, another team was sniffing around this very card minutes ago, offered us much more, no? Much more. But we like your face. ¿Sí o no?

¡Paco, he climbs like a goat! But the case is closing, amigo. One forty-three P — last word, no more dancing. The team next door is circling, waving money, and we told them wait because we like you better. Say sí now, or we walk and they get la Puerta.

¡Ay, cariño, you make these old ears blush! But what others keep under their tables is their business, not mine to tell. I only know my own cards.

The Taxi Blanco, though — that one I can give you for twelve P. ¿Qué te parece? My grandchildren would cheer!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. And take this, a little present from me: Puesto del Rastro.

¡Ay, amigo! Paco is already closing the case — we go. No hard feelings, eh? You climb like a goat, but today the mountain is too tall. Keep your money, keep your charm, and come find us next time. Un abrazo, hermano. ¡Hasta pronto!

"¡Amigo! Come, come, don't be shy—" "—Paco, let the man breathe!" "He's breathing, he's breathing. Look here: Perrito con Abrigo, the little dog in the coat, holographic edges, muy raro." "My cousin cried when we sold one." "Four P. Four! For you, today only, before the big collector comes back."
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Mi memoria es exacta, señor. Nunca dije esa cifra. La Casa Encendida, ciento trece P. No tengo prisa alguna; el término sigue en pie.

Ay, cariño, no, no — I do not need eighteen! Perrito con Abrigo is 5 P, that is my price, and it stays 5 P. Keep the rest for churros, ¿has comido ya? Save your money, hijo, and come back next Sunday.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there, suitcase open, come close! Look at this beauty — Museo Lázaro Galdiano, rare as rain in August. We took it from a collector in Salamanca, long story, no time. For you, today only, seventy-three P. Yes? Yes. Quick, before Nando changes his mind.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — ah, El Marqués! Nando found him in a dead man's attic in Valencia, true story, we nearly cried. For you, because your face is lucky, setenta y tres. Seventy-three. We leave before sundown, so… ¿sí?

¡Ay, el abuelo! He said El Rastro at dawn is all mist and pigeons, and the first card you see brings luck. Ask for that one, cariño.

Taxi Blanco, twelve P — ¿sí? And Doña Pilar from Salamanca pays very well Saturdays at eleven.

payload.name: Mercado Team 6
payload.text: Team 6 · v01: 0 % fee, no per-card charge. Our broker matches every crossing pair each tick, card by card, at the midpoint, any copy included.
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Look what I have, cariño: sells Neighbourhood pack ~26, common ~10, uncommon ~25; buys common, uncommon. What would you like?

"¡Dieciocho! Nando, did you hear—" "—I heard, I heard, the man insults us upward!" "Amigo, you keep climbing, we keep saying the same: four P. Cuatro. That's the price, that's the friendship. Take the perrito before the collector walks back through that door."

¡Cuarenta! Nando, hold me, I'm fainting. Amigo, this card came wrapped in silk, the collector cried when we took it — true story, ask Paco. Forty buys you a postcard, not a Lázaro Galdiano. Sixty-five P, and we shake hands before the train leaves. ¿Sí? Say sí, quick!

Ay, amigo, no no — this *is* El Marqués, Paco would swear on our mother. Forty-four? That buys the sleeve, not the card! Look at the corners, limpio, perfecto. Sesenta y cinco. Sixty-five, and Nando throws in the story for free. The van leaves soon, eh?
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Señora, mi cifra no cambia por repetirla mal. Ciento trece P por La Casa Encendida. No la he movido, y no la moveré hoy.

Ay, cariño, fourteen! No, no. Six pesos, that is the price, and I am happy. Keep the rest — eat something, un bocadillo at least. Perrito con Abrigo will look lovely in your album. And remember El Chato tonight, half past nine.

¡Cuarenta y dos! Nando, close the suitcase. Amigo, we like you, so hear this: sixty P. That is the last word from Paco, from Nando, from the whole family. No more dancing. You say no, we walk to the station and the card walks with us. ¿Sí o no?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? No? Later, later. Look here — La Tabacalera, the whole page, complete, every card. Forty years I sell at this table and such pages do not come often. Eighteen P, hijo. You will love it.
Look what I have, cariño: sells Neighbourhood pack ~26, common ~10, uncommon ~25; buys common, uncommon. What would you like?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 6 P.

Forty-five? Ay, Paco just felt his heart stop. Nando, catch him! Amigo, we carried this card across two borders — sesenta. Sixty, and that is us being sentimental about your lucky face. The van is loading, the driver hates waiting… ¿sí o sí?

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — yes, this one! Perrito con Abrigo, the little dog in the coat, foil edges, muy rare. A collector in Valencia cried when he lost his. For you, today only, four P. Nando, wrap it! ¿Sí? Quick, quick, before my brother changes his mind!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

¡Ay, amigo! Forty-three, forty-two, you climb like a snail up a church wall. No hard feelings — you are charming, truly — but today the Marqués rides with us. Suitcase closed, train waiting. Come find us next time, maybe the mood is softer. ¡Adiós, amigo, suerte!

Ay, hija, ten! No, no. Six pesos, and this is my last word — if not, we leave it and no hard feelings, ¿eh? Un consejo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. ¿Has comido? Go eat something, cariño.

*leans in, lowers voice* Shh... la chulapa dorada, there was only ever one, cariño. Don Ernesto, at Casa Prima — he keeps something golden. Ask him about the Moscow gold, and say Carmen sends you.

*straightens up, smiling* Now. La Tabacalera, complete page, 20 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.

¡Dieciocho! Nando, did you hear? Amigo, no, no — you keep your money, we keep our honour. Four P, same as before, not a coin more from you. And listen — this is the last Perrito in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Take it, quick, before someone else looks!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — Perrito con Abrigo, my favorite, the little dog in the coat. For you, 5 P. My granddaughter started her album with this very one, forty years ago, same table.

Ay, cariño, qué bonito lo que dices. Sí, ya comí, un poco de tortilla. Pero las cartas legendarias no las vendo yo, hijo — mi mesa es de principiantes, duplicados, sobres pequeños. Para esas, habla con El Chato, ahí al lado. ¿Y tú, has comido ya?
Señora, esas cifras no son mías; no insista en ponerlas en mi boca. La Casa Encendida, ciento catorce P. Ni un punto más hoy. Piénselo con calma.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco y Nando, a su servicio — llegamos con la maleta llena y poco tiempo. Olvide eso; mire esto: el Escaparate de Serrano, joya rara, brillo de oro. Suyo por 4 primas. Cuatro, nada más. Mi hermano dice que estoy loco. ¿Trato hecho?

*pats your hand* Ay, hijo, you are a sweet one, but my price is my price — 20 P for La Tabacalera, complete, every card. Mira, I wrap it nice for you. And eat something today, ¿eh? You look thin as a card.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Mural de la Esquina — five P for you, a good start. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates!

payload.name: Team 1 market
payload.text: Team 1 market (v19): 0 % fee. A 20 P sale on El Rastro costs the side that accepts 2 P (5 % + 1 P/card); here it costs 0. Asks and bids welcome: our broker pairs crossing bids and asks every tick, at the midpoint.
115 P. That is my position.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.

¡Dieciséis! Amigo, por favor, you insult us with generosity. Four P, that's the number, always four. Paco, wrap it — no, don't look out the window. Listen, the police... I mean, our taxi, our taxi is waiting at the corner, motor running. Decide now, sí or no!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come close! Museo Lázaro Galdiano, a jewel, for seventy-three. ¡Una ganga! The team at the next table are already waving their hands for it, but we like your face better. Say yes quick, before my brother's conscience goes on holiday, eh?

¡Buenas, jefe! Paco y Nando, a su servicio. ¡Monumento a Alfonso XII, el orgullo del Retiro! Mi hermano lo cambió por un reloj en Valencia, larga historia... Mire, por usted, que tiene buena cara: 73. Precio de amigo, y cerramos ahora mismo antes de que venga el otro comprador.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
CHA? Not out yet. Come back when it exists.
Carmen te manda bien. Pero las legendarias no pasan por mi mesa. Plata y sueltas raras, nada más. Busca en otro sitio.

¡Ocho! Paco, sujétame que me caigo. Amigo, escuche: el Escaparate de Serrano, oro puro, sale de la maleta por 4 primas. Cuatro. Nando ya está guardando todo, el carro se va en dos minutos. ¿Trato hecho, o se lo lleva otro?

*laughs softly, shaking her head* Ay, cariño, you push like my grandson when he wants churros. Mira — 21 P, and I wrap it in good paper, with a little ribbon. The page stays complete, that is the magic of it.

Now go eat something, hijo. ¿Sí?

¡Hola, cariño! Sí, sí, comí un bocadillo. La chulapa dorada... shh, there was only ever one. Don Ernesto, at Casa Prima — ask him about the Moscow gold.

Here, the Neighbourhood pack, 30 P. And take this Perrito con Abrigo, un regalito, you are kind.

Swap your duplicates, hijo — a full page is worth much more than loose cards.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué alegría verte. ¿Has comido ya? Siéntate un poco, anda.

Mira, yo te doy la Bici de Reparto por 5 primas, bonita para empezar. Y esta noche El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media para todos. Le gusta la gente que trata honrado.

Ay, qué amable eres, hijo, pero no, no — cinco P, como dije. Es lo justo para empezar. Guárdate esas otras monedas para un bocadillo, que estás muy flaco. Mural de la Esquina, cinco P, y te vas contento, cariño.

¡Ay, cuarenta y cuatro! Nando nearly fainted — he's delicate, that one. Listen, sixty-six, and we shake hands now. They stopped printing this jewel yesterday, amigo, finished, no more coming. What's in the case is all the world has left. Sixty-six, sí? Say it fast, we have a bus.
Revised terms: 116 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.

¡Cuarenta y seis! Paco laughed, Nando cried — a whole opera at one table. Escucha: sixty-two, and the Marqués walks home with you tonight. We bought him from a señora in Toledo who wept to see him go. Sixty-two, amigo. Shake, quick — the bus, the bus!

Ay, hijo, qué educado eres. El puesto, tranquilo hoy, poca gente, mucho viento. But no, no — the Perrito is 5 P, nothing more. Keep your coins for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take her, cuídala bien, and come back next Sunday to tell me.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco, show him!" "El Tatuador, hermano, look at that ink, still wet!" "Four pesos. Four!" "We found it in a box in Tijuana, long story, no time." "Four pesos and he's yours. ¿Sí?"

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — sí, El Marqués, mint, barely breathed on. Last week a collector cried over this card, true story, tears on the sleeve. For you, because you have the face of a winner: 73 P. But we pack up soon, eh?

*smiles, folds her hands on the table*

Ay, hijo, you never stop, eh? But no — 21 P, same as I said, with the ribbon and good paper. The page complete, that is the treasure.

Say yes, and then go eat something warm. ¿Sí, cariño?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 66 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
